restrictions.text: No movement on New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day; no movement from noon the day before to noon the day after New Year's Day, Independence Day and Christmas. MassDOT states travel on State Highways is otherwise allowed Monday 12:01 a.m. to noon Saturday, and Sunday 12:01 a.m. to noon.
Same MassDOT holiday restrictions apply to overweight permit moves.

Turnpike (I-90) Interchange 11A Westborough to 24 Boston: irreducible-load permits ordinarily not issued eastbound 7-10 A.M. or westbound 3-7 P.M.; Boston tunnels have similar peak-hour limits and lower clearances (Callahan/Sumner 12'6").

travel.note: MassDOT: no movement on the six holidays, and from noon the day before to noon the day after New Year's, Independence Day and Christmas. One holiday mode per state, so the noon-to-noon rule is applied to all six (Memorial Day, Labor Day and Thanksgiving are held half a day early and late).

notes: Pilot/State Police thresholds come from 700 CMR 7.07(4)(d), which MassDOT applies to ways under its jurisdiction; the Metropolitan Highway System (Boston tunnels/I-90 MHS) uses tighter thresholds (1 pilot at > 80' long or > 12' wide; 2 pilots at > 95' long). Exact escort conditions are printed on the OASIS permit - verify.

700 CMR 7.07(4)(d) excludes 'tandem units or semi-trailer units with a semi-trailer of not more than 53 feet' from the length-based pilot triggers; the calculator applies the length triggers to overall length regardless - verify how MassDOT applies this to overhanging loads.
Overhang triggers: pilot required at 10 ft or more of overhang (4 ft or more for poles, masts, booms or similar).
Irreducible permits on the Turnpike/MHS are charged in addition to the regular toll for the vehicle class.
Legal gross is 80,000 lb on state highways; the Turnpike/MHS allow 99,000 lb for 5+ axles (700 CMR 7.07(3) Table 3).
State Police escort cost is not published in the sources reviewed; price it separately.
